html:
The decisive battle of Caesar's civil war, fought on 9 August 48 BCE near Pharsalus in Thessaly, central Greece. Julius Caesar beat the much larger army of Pompey and the Senate.

Pompey had more infantry and far more cavalry, led by Titus Labienus, once Caesar's best officer. Senators in his camp pressed him to fight and finish the war. His plan was for the cavalry to sweep round Caesar's right flank. Caesar guessed it and hid a fourth line of picked cohorts behind his cavalry. When Pompey's horsemen charged, these men attacked them with their javelins, and the cavalry fled. Caesar's cohorts then rolled up Pompey's left, and his army collapsed.

Pompey rode away and fled by sea to Egypt, where he was murdered on landing. Caesar pardoned many of the men who surrendered, among them Marcus Brutus, who later helped kill him. Cicero, who had not been at the battle, also made his peace with Caesar.
sum: The decisive battle of Caesar's civil war, fought on 9 August 48 BCE near Pharsalus in Thessaly, central Greece. Julius Caesar beat the much larger army of Pompey and the Senate.
